system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-ICHEN-01 as sam.okafor and executed the specified \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1 script. A network logon shortly beforehand identifies sam.okafor and WS-SOKAFOR-01 as the source workstation.

The PowerShell activity is consistent with the described workstation-patching workflow: it accessed Windows Update through the proxy, launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package, and exited shortly afterward.

After the patch activity, ivy.chen's Firefox opened a Citrix StoreWeb portal at customer.cloud.com and made repeated requests to its page and resources, including POST requests. The supplied service inventory does not list this remote-access service as approved.
Webex.exe was launched with an app.slack.com URL, but these records do not establish that a Slack connection or session succeeded.
System processes accessed LSASS during the review window, but the supplied records do not show that credentials were extracted or otherwise establish credential dumping.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; the supplied sensor status reports collection as okay on WS-ICHEN-01 during the review window.
The records show browser requests to the Citrix portal but do not establish whether an authenticated remote session was created or what, if anything, was accessed within it.
claims_not_established: Whether ivy.chen was authorized to access the customer.cloud.com Citrix portal.
Whether the Citrix page activity resulted in a remote-access session, file transfer, or other consequential action.
Whether Slack was actually accessed; the evidence establishes only a Webex process command line containing a Slack URL.
Whether the LSASS access events involved any credential access beyond the recorded process handles.
The contents, integrity, and authorization of the patch script and the Windows update package are not established by these records.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with ivy.chen and the relevant business owner whether the customer.cloud.com Citrix portal is an authorized work resource and whether a remote session was expected.
Review Citrix authentication, session, and file-transfer logs for ivy.chen around 14:02–14:04 UTC.
Verify the deployed Apply-Updates.ps1 script and the KB5047001 update package against approved versions, signatures, and hashes.
If investigating possible credential access, obtain process-access details and relevant endpoint protection or memory telemetry for the recorded LSASS access events.
